nodes.content: Develop RLHF that preserves conflicting minority preferences under policy-induced distribution shifts without observing annotator group identities.
requirements: Improve worst-group preference win rate by ≥5 percentage points versus pooled RLHF, matching feedback budgets.
Establish identifiability conditions separating persistent preference disagreement from annotation noise under distribution shift.

nodes.content: Cluster pseudonymous annotators using repeated anchor comparisons, then train importance-weighted minimax RLHF targeting worst-cluster preference win rate under policy shifts.
Under what shared-anchor repetition and policy-support overlap are latent preference clusters identifiable separately from annotator-specific noise?
Three repeated shared anchors, independent symmetric noise below 50%, distinct cluster signatures, and positive policy overlap identify persistent disagreement.
Derive three-view anchor-mixture identifiability conditions, then test noise and policy-overlap boundaries in shifted-policy simulations.
Run ShiftMix-3 with 10,000 annotators and three anchor repeats; sweep noise 0.1–0.6 and policy overlap 0–0.2; measure cluster recovery.
ShiftMix-3: two minority-preference models matched observations; distinct anchors, three repeats, independent 10% noise, 20% marginal overlap, zero minority shifted-pair coverage.
Persistent disagreement is identifiable only with cluster-conditional shifted-pair coverage, full-rank three-view anchors, and independent noise below 50%.
Run ShiftMix-3 factorial tests varying minority shifted-pair coverage (0/10%), anchor rank, and noise (10/55%); assess identifiability.
ShiftMix-3: minority shifted-pair accuracy reached 91% with 10% coverage, full-rank anchors, 10% noise; zero coverage yielded indistinguishable models.
Reject marginal-overlap screening: 20% overlap masked minority nonidentifiability; require 10% minority shifted-pair coverage in ShiftMix-3 before minimax RLHF.
Test coverage-gated minimax RLHF across ShiftMix-3 noise/overlap sweeps, requiring 10% shifted-pair coverage per inferred cluster at matched budgets.
ShiftMix-3 v1 evaluation bundle containing matched-budget sweep results, pooled-RLHF comparisons, cluster-coverage checks, and worst-cluster win-rate scripts.
Can coverage-gated minimax RLHF gain ≥5 percentage points in worst-group win rate versus pooled RLHF with matched feedback?
Audit ShiftMix-3 v1 bundle: rerun coverage-gated minimax and pooled RLHF at matched budgets; verify coverage and five-seed worst-group gaps.
ShiftMix-3: at 10% cluster coverage, minimax RLHF averaged 62% worst-group win rate versus pooled RLHF’s 55% across five matched-budget seeds.
Using ShiftMix-3 v1 scripts, compare minimax and pooled RLHF worst-group win rates on three held-out shifts with 12,000 labels each.
Three held-out ShiftMix-3 shifts: at 10% cluster coverage and matched budgets, minimax worst-group wins were 57% versus pooled’s 55%.
Defer adoption: ShiftMix-3 gains 7 points in-distribution but only 2 on held-out shifts; prioritize shift-aware anchor acquisition.
ShiftAnchor-RLHF actively queries repeated comparisons in undercovered policy regions, then trains against the worst latent preference component.
How can ShiftAnchor-RLHF target minority-specific shifted-pair coverage without observing groups or exhausting its matched feedback budget?
Routing disputed shifted pairs to pseudonymous annotators in undercovered inferred clusters achieves 10% cluster-conditional coverage within 2,400 of 12,000 labels.
On three held-out ShiftMix-3 shifts, allocate 2,400/12,000 labels to disputed-pair routing; measure cluster coverage and matched-budget worst-group wins.
Across three ShiftMix-3 shifts, routing 2,400 labels achieved 11% minority coverage; ShiftAnchor-RLHF worst-group wins reached 61% versus pooled’s 55%.
Does 30% pseudonymous annotator turnover between anchor and shifted-pair rounds erase ShiftAnchor-RLHF’s six-point worst-group gain?
Simulate 30% annotator turnover across three held-out ShiftMix-3 shifts; measure cluster coverage and worst-group wins at 12,000 labels.
With 30% annotator turnover, minority coverage fell to 6%; ShiftAnchor-RLHF worst-group wins were 56% versus pooled’s 55%.
Conditionally adopt ShiftAnchor-RLHF for stable panels; defer turnover settings pending re-anchoring, since 30% turnover drops coverage below 10%.
BridgeAnchor-RLHF uses rotating shared comparisons to embed newcomers and replenish inferred-cluster coverage before minimax updates within 12,000-label budgets.
Can three rotating bridge comparisons per newcomer restore 10% minority shifted-pair coverage under 30% turnover within 12,000 labels?
Three rotating bridge comparisons align newcomer clusters across rounds, restoring ≥10% minority shifted-pair coverage despite 30% turnover within 12,000 labels.
Run BridgeAnchor-RLHF on three held-out ShiftMix-3 shifts with 30% turnover; count bridge labels within 12,000 and measure minority coverage.
Across three ShiftMix-3 shifts with 30% turnover, three bridges per newcomer yielded 8% minority coverage within 12,000 labels.
Replicate the three-bridge protocol across 20 new ShiftMix-3 turnover seeds; estimate minority-coverage intervals and audit missed cluster assignments.
In 20 new 12,000-label ShiftMix-3 turnover seeds, three bridges achieved ≥10% minority coverage in 17 (mean 11%).
Retain three bridges as a baseline, but require coverage checks and adaptive re-anchoring; 8% failure precludes guaranteed 10% coverage.
Can posterior cluster-coverage bounds predict 10% coverage failures early enough to re-anchor within 12,000 labels?
Calibrate posterior inferred-cluster coverage bounds; trigger newcomer bridges before 8,000 labels when projected coverage misses 10%, within 12,000 labels.
Fit 90% lower bounds for minority shifted-pair coverage on 20 turnover seeds; trigger bridges at 8,000 labels below 10%.
BridgeAnchor v0.2 coverage monitor includes 90% lower-bound estimates, an 8,000-label re-anchoring trigger, and a 12,000-label budget ledger.
Evaluate BridgeAnchor v0.2 on 30 held-out turnover seeds: measure 8,000-label failure detection, final minority coverage, and matched-budget worst-group wins.
BridgeAnchor detected 8/9 projected failures by 8,000 labels; 27/30 reached 10% coverage; worst-group wins averaged 61% versus pooled’s 55%.
Using BridgeAnchor v0.2, prospectively test alarm calibration on 50 unseen high-turnover shifts; measure missed coverage failures and matched-budget worst-group wins.
Across 50 unseen 45%-turnover shifts, BridgeAnchor missed 12/20 coverage failures; worst-group wins averaged 57% versus pooled’s 55% at 12,000 labels.
Restrict BridgeAnchor-RLHF to validated 30%-turnover settings; defer 45%-turnover deployment because missed coverage failures erase the five-point gain.
ProbeMix-RLHF reserves 20% of 12,000 labels for randomized shifted-pair probes, refreshing three-view clusters under 45% turnover.
Can randomized shifted-pair probes distinguish persistent minority disagreement from cluster-label drift under 45% annotator turnover?
Three repeated probes per newcomer align clusters if 10% minority shifted-pair coverage and full-rank anchors hold despite 45% turnover.
Randomize 2,400 probe labels across shifted pairs, estimate three-view cluster alignment, then test noise-versus-drift separation on held-out shifts.
Run ShiftMix-3 at 45% turnover, crossing noise and cluster drift; test three-view alignment and minority coverage using 2,400 triplicate-probe labels.
ShiftMix-3: at 45% turnover, 12% minority coverage, and full-rank anchors, correlated probe noise yielded observationally indistinguishable, conflicting newcomer clusters.
Randomize 2,400 split-session probes under 45% turnover; compare correlated-noise and preference-drift controls via residual dependence and cluster alignment.
Split-session probes flagged correlated noise; independent-noise, full-rank runs with 12% minority coverage aligned 90% of newcomers at 45% turnover.
Gate ProbeMix-RLHF on split-session noise-independence checks; correlated noise defeats alignment despite sufficient coverage and full-rank anchors.
Evaluate noise-gated ProbeMix-RLHF versus pooled RLHF on 50 held-out 45%-turnover shifts, counting 2,400 split-session probes within 12,000 labels.
ProbeMix v0.1 evaluation bundle records noise-gate outcomes, probe-inclusive 12,000-label ledgers, cluster alignment, and worst-group comparisons against pooled RLHF.
Does noise-gated ProbeMix-RLHF retain a ≥5-point worst-group win-rate gain at 45% turnover when probes count toward 12,000 labels?
Audit ProbeMix v0.1 across 50 held-out shifts: verify probe-inclusive budgets, noise-gate pass rates, and five-seed worst-group win gaps.
Across 38/50 noise-gate-passing 45%-turnover shifts, ProbeMix reached 61% versus pooled’s 55% worst-group wins, including probes within 12,000 labels.
Adopt ProbeMix only when split-session noise checks pass; its six-point gain applies to 38 passing shifts, not 12 rejected shifts.
DecorrAnchor-RLHF randomizes anchor paraphrases across independent annotator panels, testing for shared prompt artifacts before coverage-gated minimax training.
Can independent-panel anchor paraphrases identify shared prompt artifacts without mistaking persistent minority preferences for correlated noise?
Cross-panel paraphrase invariance flags prompt artifacts when residual agreement shifts ≥15 points while stable cluster preferences remain within 5 points.
Randomize anchor paraphrases across independent ShiftMix-3 panels; compare residual-agreement changes and minority preference stability with versus without prompt artifacts.
ShiftMix-3: shared prompt artifacts shifted residual agreement only 8 points, below the 15-point flag; minority preferences stayed within 3 points.
Across independent panels, semantically matched paraphrases flag artifacts at ≥6-point residual shifts with ≤5-point cluster-preference variation.
Test the six-point artifact flag on 100 held-out semantically matched ShiftMix-3 paraphrases; measure false positives and cluster-preference variation.
On 100 held-out ShiftMix-3 paraphrases, the six-point flag detected 42/50 artifacts; false positives were 3/50; minority variation stayed ≤4 points.
Use six-point paraphrase flags for screening, not identification: 8/50 artifacts escaped detection despite low minority-preference variation.
Can independent-panel paraphrase screening recover ≥5-point worst-group gains on ProbeMix’s 12 noise-gate-rejected shifts within 12,000 labels?
Reserve 1,200 labels for independent-panel paraphrases, exclude flagged anchors, reallocate probes, and compare matched-budget worst-group wins on 12 rejected shifts.
On 12 ProbeMix-rejected shifts, screen anchors using six-point flags, then retrain DecorrAnchor-RLHF with 1,200 paraphrase labels budgeted.
DecorrAnchor v0.1 bundle logs six-point anchor flags, 1,200 paraphrase labels within each 12,000-label budget, and retrained policies.
Audit DecorrAnchor v0.1 on 12 rejected shifts: verify 12,000-label ledgers, cluster coverage, and worst-group wins against pooled RLHF.
On 12 rejected shifts, DecorrAnchor achieved 60% worst-group wins versus pooled’s 54% at 12,000 labels; 10 shifts met coverage.
Independently rerun DecorrAnchor v0.1 policies on 24 new noise-gate-rejected shifts; audit cluster coverage and matched-budget worst-group wins.
On 24 new rejected shifts, DecorrAnchor reached 57% worst-group wins versus pooled’s 54%; only 14 shifts met 10% minority coverage.
Defer DecorrAnchor for rejected shifts: six-point screening misses artifacts, and new shifts gain only three points with unreliable coverage.
Adopt noise-gated ProbeMix for passing 45%-turnover shifts and coverage-monitored ShiftAnchor/BridgeAnchor for validated panels; defer ungated minimax and rejected shifts.
